rationale: This is a tiny (4 functions, ~1.1KB text) crypto kernel where rc4_crypt and rc4_setup are hot, tight loops, so the table favors low-cost, low-risk transformations: SUB and SPLIT get high affinity across all dimensions (cheap instruction substitution and basic-block splitting add real diversity to the RC4 key-schedule and keystream arithmetic with negligible overhead and minimal miscompilation risk), while FLA and BCF get high SecurityGain/DiversityGain but deliberately low RuntimeCost/SizeCost affinity so the feature selector applies them sparingly — primarily to main and rc4_setup rather than the per-byte keystream loop — since bogus control flow and dispatch-loop flattening would multiply execution time in the hot path and bloat a 1KB binary; IBR and ICALL take middle weights (decent security/diversity payoff from indirect branches and calls, moderate runtime/size cost, slightly lower CorrectnessRisk tolerance given pointer-heavy RC4 state indexing where indirecting references can interact badly with aliasing); IGV is weighted low across the board because this program has almost no global-variable surface to obfuscate, so it would only add size and risk without meaningful resistance gains.
